packageRules.description: Cooldown before adopting any new version. Most malicious npm releases are detected and unpublished within hours, so a delay turns the common case into a non-event. This mirrors `min-release-age=7` in .npmrc: one layer at proposal time, one at install time.

Actions are pinned to a commit SHA, which is what makes them immutable. Without automated bumping a pin rots and stops receiving security fixes, so this is the half of SHA pinning that keeps it honest.
Base images are pinned by digest for the same reason. Keep tag and digest in sync.

A dependency that executes code at install time, or that provides an executable on the build's $PATH, deserves an individual review rather than being swept into a group PR. Install-time execution is denied outright by the `allowScripts` policy, and a package that adds an executable changes what every `npm run` script resolves.
Never move off the npm major that enforces the allowScripts policy without a deliberate decision.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: A published vulnerability is the one case where waiting out the cooldown is the wrong trade.
